evidence: REFUTE checks: (a) No equivalent transition appears: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:15-17 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:152-153,165,172,179 make committed desired state the reconciler's input, while DESIGN-NOTES.md:185,189 approve cancellation of unresolved graph requests without saying whether it supersedes that state. Instance exclusions (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:24; DESIGN-NOTES.md:217-219) prevent recreation after explicit retirement but are not specified as the result of cancelling a request. (b) The accepted tradeoff is that cancellation does not assert external effects happened or were undone (DESIGN-NOTES.md:189; HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:98); it does not resolve whether still-pending effects remain desired. (c) This is within graph's own structural/reconciliation scope (DESIGN-NOTES.md:187), not external project-task cancellation. (d) Material case: activation is committed; pane creation fails during a transient Herdr outage; the unresolved graph request is cancelled; Herdr recovers. With unchanged desired activation, periodic reconciliation still calls for the pane under DESIGN-NOTES.md:165,172,179, despite the promise that cancellation ends obsolete work (line 189). A superseding mutation could settle this, but none is prescribed. Narrow finding: define whether cancellation affects committed intent or only a pending/revision request, and how the former supersedes current desired state. This is an acknowledged open detailed contract (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:149), so Should-fix design gap, not proof of implementation failure or data loss.
